topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: CPU Proximity
explanation: The memory hierarchy is a multi-level storage architecture designed to mitigate the CPU-DRAM latency gap. It arranges storage components based on speed and capacity, placing smaller, faster cache levels (L1, L2, L3) progressively closer to the CPU core. Caching strategies exploit the principle of locality of reference, moving frequently used data into these faster tiers. A cache hit results in low-latency access, whereas a cache miss requires fetching data from the next slower level, incurring a significant performance penalty. Effective cache management is essential for optimizing system throughput and instruction execution rate.
